whyNoNativeTypes: A `pure` row is evaluated inside the plan and may not touch the world (ForgeRuntime/Framework/RuntimeGraphContracts.cs refuses a pure capability that declares an entity, resource or handle port). There is therefore no type.member evidence to record for these rows; their evidence is that the declared capability equals the catalog row field for field, which ForgeTrigger/tests/Contracts asserts against the catalog file itself.

rows.hostOnly: A plan runs on the host only, so this row is evaluated there and its result reaches clients with the execution that produced it; no level seed is read and none is needed. The seed stays an explicit input because the pure tier is re-evaluable on demand and must remain a function of what the plan wrote. The deleted `forge.condition.predicate.chance` is this row compared through forge.condition.predicate.compare.

rows.format: The template is a composite format string read with the invariant culture, so `{0:0}` writes an integer, `{0:0.00}` a fixed decimal count and `{0:0%}` the value times one hundred with the percent sign. A malformed template, a template that never places the value, a result longer than the 256-character string budget and one carrying control characters are refused with this family's own codes; the website has no preview for this row yet.
